title: KPI Sidequests Playbook — Rita's micro-OKR experiments
content:
Context / purpose:
- This is my lightweight playbook for running 4–8 week micro-OKRs ("sidequests") that sit next to team OKRs. Goal is to run high-leverage, low-cost experiments that feed signals into product work and my own career learning.
- Not for formal PR review — quick notes, hypotheses, checkpoints, and a short retro at the end of each sidequest.

Northstar for the quarter:
- Weekly experiment completions (WEC): target 6 (one ~every 5–6 days).
- Signal quality > 0.6: at least 60% of experiments produce actionable follow-ups (tickets, docs, evals).

How I run a sidequest (process):
1) Hypothesis (1–2 lines) — what I want to learn or move.
2) Success criteria (quantitative if possible).
3) 2-week plan split into tiny bets (A/B style if relevant).
4) Quick eval metric + manual notes.
5) Decide: ship, scale, or shelve.

Template (copy + fill fast):
- Name: <short>
- Hypothesis: I think X because Y -> if I do Z then outcome W.
- Success: metric, baseline, target.
- Steps (week1/2 bulleted).
- Quick resources (link to any ticket or draft).
- Checkpoint 1 date / notes.
- Decision: ship/scale/shelve + next actions.

Active sidequests (current quarter):
- Micro-prompt-cache audit
  - Hypothesis: A tiny KV cache for top-queries will cut median latency for my test harness by 12–20% and reduce tokens processed in repeat queries.
  - Success: baseline median latency 210ms -> target <190ms for this harness run; evidence = two independent runs.
  - Week1: write harness, capture distributions; Week2: implement simple LRU prefix cache; Week3: run ab test; Week4: decide.
  - Checkpoint 2026-01-12: baseline captured (mean 232ms, median 210ms).
  - Checkpoint 2026-01-26: LRU cache proof-of-concept -> median 188ms, but tail occasionally spikes on cold inference. Next: add cache warm strategy.
  - Decision: iterate (add warm strategy + instrumentation).

- Personal onboarding doc for new DS interns
  - Hypothesis: a 2-page "first week" doc + 2 short notebooks reduces ramp time for basic evals by ~40% vs ad-hoc pairing.
  - Success: track time-to-first-successful-eval (TTFSE) baseline: 5 days -> target 3 days.
  - Notes: created draft, shared w/ Maya (link in linked_artifacts), need to ask SRE about data access steps.

- Weekly focus experiments (tiny habits):
  - 10-minute morning planning (days attempted this week: 4/7) — sticky but falls off during travel.
  - Weekly async Friday retro notes (2–3 bullets) — success measure: habit sustained 8 weeks -> try again next month.

Runbook fragments / tooling TODOs:
- Add a lightweight telemetry tag for any experiment I run: team=personal, sidequest=name, metric=xxx. (saves manual join later)
- Create a GitHub repo (scripts + small datasets) to avoid ephemeral local notes.
- Flows: quick checklist to create a ticket and an eval harness.

Weekly check-ins (snippets):
- 2026-02-14: Focus was prompt-cache iteration. Did 2 runs, saw warm strategy reduces tail by 30% on 99th percentile. Mood: good. Blockers: need a small infra quota for nightly runs.
- 2026-02-07: Took a day to triage experiments; shelved a low-signal idea (reranking tiny rerank pool) after 3 failed attempts. Decision: shelve + write short note about why.
- 2026-01-31: Paused habit experiment (10m planning) due to calendar chaos; regained consistency 3 days later.

Retrospective notes (rolling):
- What worked: small, time-boxed experiments force quick decisions and avoid scope creep. Sharing a 1-paragraph outcome makes me more likely to follow through.
- What didn't: I underestimate infra needs (quota, small storage) and that kills momentum. Need an "infra precheck" step.
- Improvements: pre-declare success criteria in metric terms; set a calendar probe (1 hour block) for experiment runs so travel doesn't squash it.

Open questions / friction points:
- How to capture qualitative signal cheaply? (currently manual notes in this doc — want quick survey template or Slack reaction collection?)
- How to tag these artifacts so eng teams can find and adopt them? (maybe prefix with personal/ in repo + add to Confluence index)
- Does RDW Infra want me to schedule quota bumps for nightly micro-runs or should I use ephemeral GPU spot runs? Need to ask infra (Slack: #infra-requests).

Tiny running backlog (one-liners):
- quick eval harness for made-up edge prompts (small dataset)
- compare quantization profile: q4 vs q8 for my tiny test model (cost delta)
- write short "failed experiment" template (1 paragraph why + 1 graph)
- extract 5 lessons from each sidequest and post weekly to #team-hacks

Decisions to make this week:
- Add telemetry tags and create a tiny repo for artifacts (high priority).
- File one infra request for a dedicated nightly run slot (medium priority).
- Convert onboarding doc to a 1-pager checklist (low priority — pair with Maya).

Notes to self:
- When stuck, cut scope by 50% and make a measurement you can do in <= 90 minutes.
- Keep the habit: force a 5-minute headline at the end of the day.

Links / references (quick):
- Confluence index: CONFLUENCE-1234 (linked_artifacts)
- GitHub gist with experiment runner: https://github.com/rita-cho/kpi-sidequests/gist/aa12bb
- Slack thread: #personal-hacks (pinned messages)

Last tiny retro (2026-02-20):
- WEC this month: 5 (close to target of 6). Signal quality approx 0.67.
- Wins: prompt-cache POC good signal; onboarding doc draft appreciated by Maya.
- Next sprint: finalize repo + short infra request + schedule two 90-minute blocks next week for runs.

-- end --
